preconditions.expression: n >= 1 and m >= 1 and all(1 <= q <= 10**5 and 1 <= w <= 10**5 for q, w in coupons)
preconditions.description: Input consists of integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^6) and m (1 ≤ m ≤ 10^5), followed by m distinct coupon pairs (q_i, w_i) where 1 ≤ q_i, w_i ≤ 10^5. All q_i are distinct.

preconditions.expression: len(coupons) == m and all(q != q2 for (q, _), (q2, _) in zip(coupons, coupons[1:]))
preconditions.description: The coupons list contains exactly m distinct q_i values.

postconditions.description: Output is a single integer representing the maximum total cost Sereja can pay, computed as the sum of w_i for all q_i present in the constructed beautiful array.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(array) <= n for array in possible_arrays) and all(all(x == y or (x, y) in adjacent_pairs or (y, x) in adjacent_pairs for x in array for y in array if x != y) for array in possible_arrays for adjacent_pairs in possible_adjacent_pairs(array))
postconditions.description: For any valid beautiful array of length n, every pair of distinct elements (x, y) in the array must appear as adjacent elements in at least one order (x followed by y or y followed by x) in the array.

postconditions.expression: max_cost == max(sum(w for q, w in coupons if q in array) for array in possible_arrays if 1 <= len(array) <= n and is_beautiful(array))
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum possible sum of w_i for q_i present in any beautiful array of length n, where a beautiful array satisfies the adjacency condition for all distinct pairs.
